title: Ben Affleck Raved About Robert Pattinson’s ‘The Odyssey’ Performance, Recalls Matt Damon: He Said ‘It Was Like Watching a Guy Run Into an Avalanche’
description:
Starring in four major movies just this year, Robert Pattinson’s star power has been put to the test, and even Ben Affleck is noticing.

	After see
body:
Starring in four major movies just this year, Robert Pattinson’s star power has been put to the test, and even Ben Affleck is noticing.

	After seeing Christopher Nolan’s “The Odyssey” for the first time, the actor consulted his close friend and star of the film, Matt Damon, to discuss Pattinson’s performance as Antinous, the antagonistic ringleader of Penelope’s suitors.

	“Ben Affleck probably talked to me for 20 minutes about just Rob after he saw the movie,” Damon said during a screening event for the film at the David Geffen Theater in the Academy Museum on Saturday night (via EW). “When they talk about a brave performance — Ben goes, ‘You had the benefit of all of the might and power of Christopher Nolan storytelling at your back’ and I went, ‘Yeah.’”
	

	Damon continued, “And he goes, ‘Rob had all of the weight and heft and power of Christopher Nolan’s storytelling coming down on him. And the way he did it, it was like watching a guy run into an avalanche.’”

	Damon agreed with Affleck’s praise, adding, “Any moment that he could be more cowardly, more hateable, you could see his wheels turning: ‘How could I make this even worse for myself?’ And it was so fun to watch because he’s such a dynamic actor and so interesting.”

	The Greek epic was not the first time Pattinson has explored Nolan’s power and storytelling. He also starred in the 2020 sci-fi action thriller “Tenet,” playing the mysterious operative Neil. Pattinson’s other projects this year include Lance Oppenheim’s “Primetime,” the dark romantic comedy “The Drama” and “Dune: Part Three,” which comes out Dec. 18.

schema.headline: Ben Affleck Raved About Robert Pattinson’s ‘The Odyssey’ Performance, Recalls Matt Damon: He Said ‘It Was Like Watching a Guy Run Into an Avalanche’

title: Box Office: Domestic Ticket Sales Up 20% From Last Year as Hollywood Awaits ‘Hunger Games’ Prequel, ‘Dune 3’ and ‘Avengers: Doomsday’
description: It’s been a triumphant year for movie theater owners, who are basking in the long-awaited box office rebound. Domestic ticket sales are already 20%
body:
It’s been a triumphant year for movie theater owners, who are basking in the long-awaited box office rebound. Domestic ticket sales are already 20% above the same point in 2025, and that’s before a “Hunger Games” prequel, a third “Dune” and another “Avengers” installment hit the big screen.

	With revenues at $8.76 billion through Nov. 15, according to Rentrak, the industry is poised to exceed $10 billion in North America for the first time since the pandemic upended the theatrical business. Prior to COVID, yearly ticket sales were regularly nearing or surpassing the $11 million mark. In the past half-decade, though, revenues have stalled below $9 billion, with receipts tapping out at $8.87 billion in 2025 and $8.7 billion in 2024 and $8.91 billion in 2023. This year, returns eclipsed $8 billion by October, a milestone the industry didn’t reach until December last year.
	

	Despite the popularity of premium large formats like Imax, which have higher prices, attendance has yet to return to pre-pandemic levels. North American revenues remain 9% behind 2019, the last “normal” period at the box office.

	“While we’re still working to close the gap with the pre-pandemic marketplace, we’re now less than 10% behind 2019 at the same point on the calendar,” says Rentrak’s head of marketplace trends Paul Dergarabedian. “That’s pretty significant, particularly given how much the theatrical marketplace has changed over the past seven years.”

	Holiday offerings like Lionsgate’s “The Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping,” which is expected to debut above $100 million prior to Thanksgiving, as well as a pair of Christmas tentpoles in Warner Bros. sequel “Dune Part Three” and Disney’s Marvel epic “Avengers: Doomsday,” should help to shrink the deficit. Other potential hits on the calendar include Universal’s starry comedy “Focker in Law” and Sony’s action threequel “Jumanji: Open World.” 
	

	“With ‘Hunger Games,’ along with the Thanksgiving corridor and a very important December still ahead, there’s a real opportunity to continue building on that momentum,” Dergarabedian adds.

	This year has been defined by unexpected triumphs, including Amazon MGM’s space epic “Project Hail Mary,” Lionsgate’s musical biopic “Michael,” A24’s psychological thriller “Backrooms” and the Focus Features horror film “Obsession.” Meanwhile, the anticipated blockbusters like Christopher Nolan’s Homer adaptation “The Odyssey” and Sony’s Marvel adventure “Spider-Man: Brand New Day” far exceeded projections, with $1.8 billion and $2.5 billion, respectively. After a record-breaking summer, the fall was comparatively light. However, the season has managed to field some unlikely winners, most notably A24’s electric Elizabeth Holmes documentary “You Can See Everything” with $89 million domestically to date. Those victories have offset the misses, including Tom Cruise’s satire “Digger,” Disney’s live-action “Moana” and Amazon MGM’s toy-inspired “Masters of the Universe.”

	“It’s the movies and the marketing that matter more than anything to general audiences,” Dergarabedian says. “And this year has demonstrated what can happen when audiences have an eclectic mix of films to see on the big screen.”

schema.headline: Box Office: Domestic Ticket Sales Up 20% From Last Year as Hollywood Awaits ‘Hunger Games’ Prequel, ‘Dune 3’ and ‘Avengers: Doomsday’

title: Phil Collins Says He’s a ‘Well Man’ Now and Hints at the ‘Possibility of Doing Some Shows’ Amid Health Battle: ‘You Haven’t Heard the Last of Me’
description: Phil Collins made a rare public appearance to accept his induction into the Rock & Roll Hall of Fame at the ceremony in Los Angeles on Saturday, wh
body:
Phil Collins made a rare public appearance to accept his induction into the Rock & Roll Hall of Fame at the ceremony in Los Angeles on Saturday, where he addressed his health, calling himself “a well man now.”

	“Thank you so much. Thank you. I’m really not as bad as it looks. I’m much better,” Collins said at the beginning of his speech. “I’ve got to say, there are lots of rumors about whether I’m going to sing, do a tour of an album, but you haven’t heard the last of me,” he added. 
	

	In the press room after the ceremony, he explained that he has an in-house recording studio and a band of fellow musicians that make it possible — and even enjoyable — for him to keep making music. He hopes to share this music and tour down the road.

	“Everything started to go wrong,” the musician said. “So at one point I didn’t think I’d live, let alone go on the road again. But just the other night I was talking to the kids about it, and everyone got excited, including myself, that it’s not beyond the realm of possibility of doing some shows.”

	“I’ve got some great friends of mine that are great musicians that have been in my band. And I’d like to get down to my studio just to have some fun and write some music that I hope will be good enough for people to hear and sort of enjoy,” he added. “So it’s a work in progress.”

	Collins has often been open about his health issues. He told The Times of London in August that he almost died in 2024 from health complications stemming from alcohol abuse. In early 2026, he told BBC Two that he’s undergone five surgeries on his knee.
	

	Despite his health challenges, he is determined to continue his music career. “Well, you say something once and you gotta answer questions about it forever. I can’t believe that I’m not going to do something. I’m not very good at doing nothing,” Collins told reporters.

schema.headline: Phil Collins Says He’s a ‘Well Man’ Now and Hints at the ‘Possibility of Doing Some Shows’ Amid Health Battle: ‘You Haven’t Heard the Last of Me’

title: Box Office: Johnny Depp’s ‘Ebenezer’ Opens to No. 1 With $19 Million, ‘How to Rob a Bank’ Stumbles With $5 Million Debut
description: Johnny Depp returned to the top of box office charts as “Ebenezer,” his new take on “A Christmas Carol,” collected a decent $19 million from 3,535
body:
Johnny Depp returned to the top of box office charts as “Ebenezer,” his new take on “A Christmas Carol,” collected a decent $19 million from 3,535 North American theaters in its opening weekend.

	Overseas, the PG-13 adaptation of the Charles Dickens classic has generated $23 million from 63 markets for a global start of $42 million.

	“Ebenezer” is notable as Depp’s first major movie role in eight years, since 2018’s “Fantastic Beasts: The Crimes of Grindelwald.” His career in Hollywood began to unravel in 2020 after allegations of domestic abuse leveled by his ex-wife Amber Heard (which he has denied) resulted in two costly, high-profile defamation trials. Although his acting roles mostly dried up, a study conducted by the National Research Group in April 2026 indicated that Depp remained a popular figure across the globe. Participants ranked him among the top 10 actors — ahead of Tom Hanks and behind Margot Robbie — who “would make you most interested in seeing a new movie in a cinema in the future.” 
	

	So how did that enthusiasm translate to “Ebenezer” in its first weekend of release? Analysts say tickets didn’t signal a resounding embrace amid Depp’s return to studio fare. However, the movie delivered a nice boost to theater owners ahead of Thanksgiving and looks to provide a sizable return on investment for Paramount. Given the uncertainty around Depp, the studio cautiously spent $38 million to produce the film. Depp was paid $5 million, a fraction of what he’s earned on prior studio movies, with the promise of bonuses tied to box office performance.
	

	“This is a solid opening for a Christmas-themed movie,” says David A. Gross, who publishes the box office newsletter FranchiseRe. “Johnny Depp remains a major celebrity around the world, and director Ti West brings some edge.”

	Directed by West, known for the “X” horror trilogy, “Ebenezer” spins the oft-told tale of the cold-hearted businessman known as Scrooge as he’s visited by the ghosts of Christmas past, present and future. Though critics were harsh (it holds a 53% on Rotten Tomatoes), audiences awarded the movie a positive “A-” grade on CinemaScore exit polls. Ticket buyers were mostly older white women; audiences were 52% female and 58% Caucasian while 59% were aged 30 or older. The movie performed best in the south, per the studio. Around 50% of moviegoers cited Depp as a reason for attending, making him the film’s top attendance driver, according to PostTrak data.

	In the wake of “Ebenezer,” box office watchers believe the town will be more willing to work with Depp. His next film is Lionsgate’s 2027 action thriller “Day Drinker,” co-starring Penélope Cruz. Meanwhile Disney has been contemplating another “Pirates of the Caribbean” movie. Depp has said he’s open to returning to the franchise as the chaotic Captain Jack Sparrow, but he noted “the only involvement I really want to have, truly, is just to send them off on a better note.”

	“With the No. 1 film in the marketplace, and his image and likeness splashed all over the marketing material, Johnny Depp’s Hollywood exile is effectively over,” says Jeff Bock, an analyst with Exhibitor Relations. “This benchmark tells the industry that Depp is once again castable, marketable and capable of opening a studio movie. Captain Jack Sparrow — it’s time to set sail again.”

	Two other movies, Amazon MGM’s caper “How to Rob a Bank” and Sony’s action thriller “Ghost Soldier,” starring Jim Caviezel, opened nationwide to mixed results. 

	“How to Rob a Bank” didn’t make bank, stumbling at No. 7 with $5 million from 2,810 theaters in its debut. It also struggled internationally with $5.1 million from 73 territories, bringing its global total to a soft $10.3 million. The heist comedy, starring Nicholas Hoult, Zoë Kravitz and Pete Davidson, was produced for more than $40 million, and cinema operators keep about half of ticket sales. What’s troubling is neither critics nor audiences were receptive to the film, which landed a “B-” grade on CinemaScore and tepid 33% on Rotten Tomatoes. David Leitch directed the R-rated movie, which follows a crew of social media-savvy bank robbers who broadcast their daring heists, unaware their viral fame has caught the attention of the feds. 
	

	“This is a weak opening for an original action comedy,” says Gross. “With limited business overseas, the movie is going to fall short of recouping its investment.”

	“Ghost Soldier” was just ahead on box office charts, in sixth place with $5.2 million over the traditional weekend and $8.3 million through its first five days of release. There’s no CinemaScore, so it’s unclear how audiences felt about the movie; reviews were negative, with a 36% on Rotten Tomatoes. “Ghost Soldier,” featuring Caviezel as a former American Special Forces soldier, carries a lean $18 million production budget.

	“How to Rob a Bank” and “Ghost Solider” opened behind several holdovers, including Warner Bros. Animation’s “The Cat in the Hat” and Gkids action sequel “Godzilla Minus Zero.” 

	“The Cat in the Hat” remained in second place with $11 million from 4,003 theaters in its sophomore outing, a 45% decline from its debut. So far, the animated family film has earned $36.7 million domestically and just $55 million globally, a disappointing tally against a $92 million budget. 

	“Godzilla Minus Zero” slid to No. 3 after leading box office charts last weekend. The kaiju sequel earned $8.31 million from 3,264 locations, a harsh 75% drop from its opening. Despite a big decline, “Godzilla Minus Zero” has been a hit in North America with $48.1 million to date.

	In fifth place, A24’s Elizabeth Holmes documentary “You Can See Everything” brought in $5.4 million from 1,845 screens in its fifth weekend of release. The buzzy movie, directed by Nathan Fielder and Lance Oppenheim, has been a huge draw with $89 million and will soon clear the $100 million mark in North America. That’s a rare box office milestone for any documentary — especially one that’s nearly three hours long.

	At No. 8, Searchlight’s dark comedy “Wild Horse Nine” added $4.6 million while expanding to 2,175 theaters. The Oscar hopeful, starring John Malkovich and Sam Rockwell and directed by Martin McDonagh, has grossed $13.3 million in North America and $28 million worldwide after two weekends in theaters. McDonagh’s prior film, 2022’s “The Banshees of Inisherin,” ended its run with $10.5 million domestically and $50 million globally. 

	Among specialty releases, A24’s heartwarming comedy “Club Kid” and Amazon MGM’s drama “I Play Rocky” attempted to sustain momentum in limited release. 
	

	“Club Kid” stayed strong with $756,060 on 27 screens, translating to $28,002 per screen and boosting its tally to $1.45 million. About 80% of audiences were under 35, according to PostTrak. Jordan Firstman wrote, directed and stars in the film, which revolves around a hard-partying club promoter who finds out he has a 10-year-old son. 

	“I Play Rocky” captured $503,818 from 29 venues, averaging $17,373 per location. Directed by Peter Farrelly, the movie depicts the real-life story of Sylvester Stallone bringing the 1976 classic “Rocky” to the big screen. Both films will expand nationwide around Thanksgiving.

	Neon’s period drama “Paper Tiger” opened to $215,009 from six screens, averaging $35,835 per location. By comparison, “Club Kid” earned $65,097 per location and “I Play Rocky” captured $49,200 per location last weekend from similar theater counts. James Gray directed the film, in which Adam Driver and Miles Teller portray brothers Irwin and Gary Pearl, whose get-rich-quick scheme to help clean up the Gowanus Canal lands them in the crosshairs of the Russian mafia.

	Overall, the box office is 20% ahead of the same point last year, and exhibitors are optimistic about the rest of November. Next weekend brings Lionsgate’s “Hunger Games” prequel “Sunrise on the Reaping,” which is tracking to open above $100 million. Then Turkey Day will bring Universal’s comedy “Focker in Law,” with Ariana Grande joining Ben Stiller and Robert De Niro, and Disney’s animated “Hexed.”

	These movies are “setting the table for what promises to be an exciting Thanksgiving frame,” says Rentrak’s head of marketplace trends Paul Dergarabedian. “With the holiday moviegoing season getting underway, the industry has a great opportunity to build momentum heading into the final weeks of the year.”

title: Rock & Roll Hall of Fame Ceremony Gets Fired Up With Live-Wire Numbers From U2, the Chili Peppers, Usher, Cynthia Erivo, Sienna Spiro, Aerosmith and More
description: You could feel it in the air that night, at the Rock & Roll Hall of Fame induction ceremony, held Saturday at L.A. Peacock Theatre and filmed for a
body:
You could feel it in the air that night, at the Rock & Roll Hall of Fame induction ceremony, held Saturday at L.A. Peacock Theatre and filmed for a December ABC special. The show’s producers would relish, as always, the thought of having younger artists salute their elders, or  bringing together some powerhouse teamings, coming up with admirably savvy ideas to make sure most of the honorees got their interesting due, regardless of whether they’d survived to make it to this point or felt it was worth the trip if they had. 
	

	To wit: Cynthia Erivo and Travis Barker joining forces as a duo truly no one saw coming for a salute to the ailing Phil Collins. Usher channeling the late Luther Vandross. St. Vincent and an all-star metal crew, including Metallica members, rocking out in honor of the absent Iron Maiden. Sienna Spiro bringing the breeziness for the also-absent Sade. Country-rock upstart Stephen Wilson Jr. honoring the most notorious no-shows of the evening, Oasis with an unexpectedly swampy approach to Britpop revivalism. 

	And then there was superproducer Rick Rubin, who got a big spotlight as an inductee but was obviously not about to perform, so showrunners came up with a novel pairing in his honor, matching the Red Hot Chili Peppers with… Rubin’s beard. Each of the RHCP members had lifelike facsimiles of Rubin’s flowing hirsuteness, with the fake beards glued on well enough to withstand a lot of headbanging, looking like a small army of prowling Zen masters.



	

					Chad Smith, Flea, Anthony Kiedis and John Frusciante of Red Hot Chili Peppers perform onstage at The 2026 Rock & Roll Hall of Fame Induction Ceremony on November 14, 2026 in Los Angeles, California. (Photo by Gilbert Flores/Variety)
									Variety
	



	That is not to neglect the inductees who were able to salute themselves — primarily, the hip-hop wing of the class of 2026: Queen Latifah, MC Lyte and Wu Tang Clan. Billy Idol was also present and accounted for in an climactic segment that saw him joined by one of his presenters, Gwen Stefani, as well as longtime cohort Steve Stevens. And there was a hybrid approach for the Joy Division/New Order performance homage, as members of the Deftones and Chvrches joined the one band representative on hand, Peter Hook to sub in for the band members from whom he is deeply estranged and/or are known to be ill.
	

	And, to bookend the four-and-a-half-hour proceedings, the Hall booked two acts — or three — who had no direct tie to this year’s proceedings but are always worth a tribute, self-honoring or otherwise: U2 opened the show with two numbers, one old and one hot off the presses. And Aerosmith and Run-DMC closed it with a reprise of the “Walk This Way” reunion that just two weeks ago closed an Aerosmith comeback at the Hollywood Bowl.



	

					Bono and The Edge of U2 perform onstage at The 2026 Rock & Roll Hall of Fame Induction Ceremony on November 14, 2026 in Los Angeles, California. (Photo by Gilbert Flores/Variety)
									Variety
	



	The U2 kickoff came as a surprise… or at least a surprise to anyone who hadn’t spent much time thinking about how much promotional activity the group was already putting in in the past week to set up the release of their first full new album in nine years, “Carnaval de Luz.” The newly re-intact foursome, with drummer Larry Mullen Jr. back in the lineup, performed the new release’s “Silencio” while flanked by men dressed as policemen holding riot shields, who mostly stood in witness to the fresh track before suddenly and alarmingly running laps around the band. Somewhat soothingly, the intimidating lawmen disappeared as the band segued into the familiar sounds of “Pride (In the Name of Love).”

	The first honoree, MC Lyte, who got in under the auspices of the Early Influence category, was inducted by Remy Ma, and in her own speech described herself as a “B-girl from Brooklyn looking for my chance to inspire and motivate a generation of people.” She did not perform, at the time, but it turned out her live rapping turn would come later, in tandem with Queen Latifah’s. 

	Oprah Winfrey was the designated sharer of the love for the late Luther Vandross, with, among the extolled values, the contention that “Luther never once over-sang a feeling.” Following her to channel Vandross, Usher performed a medley of “Here and Now,” “So Amazing” and (a title that seemed to echo Oprah’s comments about not oversinging) “Never Too Much.”



	

					Oprah Winfrey speaks onstage at The 2026 Rock & Roll Hall of Fame Induction Ceremony on November 14, 2026 in Los Angeles, California. (Photo by Gilbert Flores/Variety)
									Variety
	





	

					Usher performs onstage at The 2026 Rock & Roll Hall of Fame Induction Ceremony on November 14, 2026 in Los Angeles, California. (Photo by Gilbert Flores/Variety)
									Variety
	



	Phil Collins, whose debilitations in recent years have long been a matter of public record, took the stage with a cane and proclaimed, half in jest, that his condition is “really not as bad as it looks.” He also made a claim that “you haven’t heard the last of me,” before Erivo and Barker made sure that the drum fill from “In the Air Tonight” got a proper airing, even as the “Wicked” star went a prodigiously long way toward reminding the world that the song has a melody, too, as well as being eternal air-drum bait.
	



	

					Phil Collins, Cynthia Erivo and Travis Barker at The 2026 Rock & Roll Hall of Fame Induction Ceremony on November 14, 2026 in Los Angeles, California. (Photo by Mark Von Holden/Variety)
									Variety
	



	Collins made a trip back to the press room at the Peacock, with few-holds-barred talk about what has been afflicting him and prospects for any musical future following his long break. “In terms of playing live, I think my drumming days are probably done,” he told the assembled press, stating what may be the obvious. “I had a really bad knee, left knee, that I had five operations on — It was replaced five times, and that meant I was in hospital for quite a while. Then my kidneys started failing and liver started failing. Everything started to go wrong, so at one point, I didn’t think I’d live, let alone go on the road again. “

	Collins continued, “But just the other night, I was talking to the kids about it, and everyone got excited, including myself, that it’s not beyond the realms of possibility of doing some shows. You know, I’ve got some great friends of mine that are great musicians that have been in my band, and I’d like to get down to my studio just to sort of have  some fun, and write some music that I hope will be good enough for people to hear and enjoy. So it’s a work in progress.”



	

					Chris Rock speaks onstage during the 2026 Rock & Roll Hall of Fame Induction Ceremony at Peacock Theater on November 14, 2026 in Los Angeles, California.  
									Getty Images for RRHOF
	



	Presenter Chris Rock said that the Wu-Tang Clan “didn’t leave Staten Island, they took it with them.” Tje collective’s extended membership filled a significant portion of the stage, so it wasn’t surprising when producers finally cut the mics just as another member was stepping up to speak. Inspectah Deck got most of the talking in, exclaiming, “I partied with Billy Idol,” then getting serious by saying, “Of course, we had our talent, but we had a village, so I want to take a moment to thank some of those people from our village.” He then ran through the names of 40 individuals or organizations, none of which will be included on the ABC broadcast, if it surely did make for a lot of returned gratitude in the room. The group was the first artist of the night to perform on their own behalf, with a seven-song medley that began with “Triumph” and climaxed with “Protect Ya Neck.”
	



	

					Chris Rock and inductees Masta Killa, Method Man, RZA and Raekwon of Wu-Tang Clan speak onstage during the 2026 Rock & Roll Hall of Fame Induction Ceremony at Peacock Theater on November 14, 2026 in Los Angeles, California. 
									Getty Images for RRHOF
	



	None of the members of Sade, the band, made it to the ceremony, including their same-named frontwoman, but that segment had all the starpower it needed with a performance of “Smooth Operator” by Sienna Spiro, whom many consider the frontrunner to win the best new artist Grammy about 300 feet away in three months.



	

					Sienna Spiro performs onstage at The 2026 Rock & Roll Hall of Fame Induction Ceremony on November 14, 2026 in Los Angeles, California. (Photo by Gilbert Flores/Variety)
									Variety
	



	Neither was there any sign of Oasis, with Noel Gallagher reportedly having booked a side gig for the night as an excuse to be antisocial, and Liam, who has frequently badmouthed the Hall, not needing any such excuse. Presenter Bob Odenkirk talked about how he would play Oasis to get in the mood for her role as Saul Goodman, calling the band “a dose of Viagra for the ego.” Country star Wilson did “Wonderwall” as a solo artist, with the show producers presumably hoping for a wave of viewer approval for his unusual take that would be similar to the massive kudos he got for singing a similarly stripped-down “Stand by Me” on the CMAs last year.

	The most hilarious immediate juxtaposition of the night? That would be Neil Young, offering a 14-minute speech in support of his friend Rick Rubin, followed by the superstar producer coming out and giving the shortest speech in Rock Hall history: “You can’t kill rock ‘n’ roll.” 



	

					Neil Young speaks onstage during the 2026 Rock & Roll Hall of Fame Induction Ceremony at Peacock Theater on November 14, 2026 in Los Angeles, California. 
									Getty Images for RRHOF
	





	

					 Inductee Rick Rubin speaks onstage during the 2026 Rock & Roll Hall of Fame Induction Ceremony at Peacock Theater on November 14, 2026 in Los Angeles, California. 
									Getty Images for RRHOF
	



	Young’s speech — again, only a tiny sliver of which is likely to make it to the TV special — consisted mostly of two recurring themes: (1) A list of the great artists Rubin has produced, by decade (though he left out Jay-Z), including an explanation of the Chicks having changed their name. (2) Thank-yous not just to producers and engineers but to the other helpers who purportedly stand guard in studio parking lots, to make sure label executives and other bean-counters are not allowed in to disturb the creative vibes.
	

	Then the Chili Peppers did “Give It Away,” getting a fresh start on it after an initial technical snafu, each and every member with a long, gray, fake beard that must have tickled all their bare chests. (Drummer Chad Smith did not get to take the rest of the night off at that point, as he returned at the very end as Aerosmith’s fill-in drummer of the moment.)



	

					 Inductee Peter Hook of Joy Division / New Order speaks onstage during the 2026 Rock & Roll Hall of Fame Induction Ceremony at Peacock Theater on November 14, 2026 in Los Angeles, California. 
									Getty Images for RRHOF
	



	Peter Hook appeared very happy to be on hand as the sole representative of one of the most fractured and ongoingly fractious bands in all of rock, New Order. “I’ve been happy, I’ve been mad and I’ve been heartbroken in equal measure,” Hook said — feelings that anyone who has read his entertainingly forthright interviews well knows — “but I’m still fucking here.” He talked about long-gone founder Ian Curtis — “The last letter I had was from him, he said, ‘I’m swirling down into a dark void'” — and talked about going into the chrysalis that became the spinoff band: “We went to New York and we were introduced to American club life. It was an exciting, brand new world. We started experimenting with electronic beats and with sequence lines and synthesizers, and that became a new direction for New Order. … ‘Blue Monday’ sounds like it was recorded yesterday. It still sounds like the future.” Then he took to center stage to share it with Deftones and Chvches’ Lauren Mayberry on a song for each of his newly inducted bands, Joy Division’s signature song “Love Will Tear Us Apart” and New Order’s “Bizarre Love Triangle.”

	Presenting to the bands generally, and to Hook specifically, was Trent Reznor, who said that in the punk era Joy Division differed by “level(ing) their gaze at the physical and emotional scars caused by the worst events of the 20th century, reflected in the industrial landscape they  called home and posed the question: What chance does love have of surviving in a place like this?” The Nine Inch Nails auteur spoke of Curtis as “one of popular music’s all-time great baritone singers. But being possessed of great sensitivity, his voice was pushed to the point where it often felt like it might break apart and descend.” After his suicide, said Reznor, the lineup that was redubbed New Order “took what had been previously breathtakingly monochrome and via the introduction of electronics rendered it in vivid color. And for the 45 years since, they’ve dedicated themselves joyfully to the conundrum of combining rock and dance, creating a blueprint for radical euphoria along the way.” (Although Hook might have had a rejoinder to that about whether the half-century was all joyful.)
	



	

					Trent Reznor and Inductee Peter Hook of Joy Division / New Order speak onstage during the 2026 Rock & Roll Hall of Fame Induction Ceremony at Peacock Theater on November 14, 2026 in Los Angeles, California. 
									Getty Images for RRHOF
	



	“I must have watched Jonathan Demme’s video for ‘The Perfect Kiss’ a thousand times,” Hook continued. “It feels to me like I’m getting to live this dream In that film, I see a curiosity, naivety, and a sense of utter conviction that always leaves me wanting to try to be fearless and try something new, to ignore the rules and reconsider what’s possible.”

	Queen Latifah said that her initial music was “mostly beats and rhymes. But I had songs in my heart. I loved reggae music. I loved salsa. Shout out to Señora Cruz” — Celia Cruz, that is, who was being posthumously inducted this year. “I loved reggae. I loved house music. I loved jazz, and I wanted to put all of that, and rock,  into my hip-hop.” Acknowledging the rarity of women in the genre, she said, “Thank you to my sisters in the name of hip-hop. If it wasn’t for (MC) Lyte, I don’t know if I would’ve known this was really possible, but when I heard Lyte rap, I was like, ‘Yo, what is that? I wanna do that.'” In conclusion, she wanted to “leave you with a quote from Maya Angelou, who said, ‘Life is not measured by the number of breaths we take, but by the moments that take our breath away.'”



	

					Megan Thee Stallion and Inductee Queen Latifah speak onstage during the 2026 Rock & Roll Hall of Fame Induction Ceremony at Peacock Theater on November 14, 2026 in Los Angeles, California. 
									Getty Images for RRHOF
	



	Latifah, who has been widely seen and heard from in recent years as an actress and singer, did her part to take breath away with a spirited return to her roots in the performance segment that followed, where she performed “U.N.I.T.Y.,” “Latifah’s Had It Up 2 Here” and — joined by MC Lyte, presenter Meghan Thee Stallion and Remy Ma — a quartet-powered “Ladies First.”



	

					(L-R) Inductee MC Lyte, Inductee Queen Latifah, and Megan Thee Stallion perform onstage during the 2026 Rock & Roll Hall of Fame Induction Ceremony at Peacock Theater on November 14, 2026 in Los Angeles, California. 
									Getty Images for RRHOF
	



	Not surprisingly, the final acceptance speech and final performance slot for an actual nominee was reserved for Idol, who has been arguably the most enthusiastic of anyone about his induction. He was introduced by No Doubt’s Stefani and Tony Kanal, with Stefani getting personal as she recalled “in ’84 taking the bus to Huntington Beachm and everybody had a boom box, and everybody at the entire beach was listening to ‘Eyes Without a Face.’ And it was pure euphoria. I didn’t know what the song meant, but it didn’t matter because it was weirdly hopeful, crazy, and dreamy and the feelings that I needed to have as a teenager. And then we saw him on MTV. The spiked hair, the leather jackets, the fingerless gloves, and the signature lip curl made him visually unforgettable. He was handsome. He was stylish. He was crazy-sexy and perfectly rebellious.”
	



	

					Gwen Stefani and Inductee Billy Idol perform onstage during the 2026 Rock & Roll Hall of Fame Induction Ceremony at Peacock Theater on November 14, 2026 in Los Angeles, California. 
									Getty Images for RRHOF
	



	Steve Stevens gave an initial thank-you speech, followed by Idol offering recollections going all the way back to his Generation X Brit-punk days. He offered encouragement “to all the young people out there who can barely tune a guitar or work a sampler: now it’s your turn. Go make the impossible possible. Find out who you are and be it. Dream, baby, dream. Keep your dreams burning forever. And now I’m gonna party with the Wu Tang Clan!” he exulted, echoing that unit’s earlier expressed enthusiasm about joining Idol’s off-stage party.



	

					Inductee Billy Idol performs onstage during the 2026 Rock & Roll Hall of Fame Induction Ceremony at Peacock Theater on November 14, 2026 in Los Angeles, California. 
									Getty Images for RRHOF
	



	The denouement, rather than an all-star jam of the likes that used to end Hall ceremonies, had Aerosmith beginning to play “Walk This Way,” with Tyler interrupting it to say something was missing — Run-DMC, who came out to thereafter do the MTV-familiar version of the track that is dominated by their contribution. It was familiar to anyone who saw the two artists do a combo version of their classic at the second of the two “Aerosmith & Friends” concerts at the Bowl on Nov. 1. As was noted at the time, Tyler sounds in surprisingly good voice for someone whose vocal issues put a halt to touring a few years ago. In celebrating the historic meeting of rock and rap that occurred in the 1980s, the closing number had plenty of symbolic import, with three hip-hop acts having been inducted earlier in the evening.



	

					Darryl McDaniels, Steven Tyler, Joseph “Rev Run” Simmons, Chad Smith and Joe Perry of Run-D.M.C., Aerosmith and Red Hot Chili Peppers perform onstage at The 2026 Rock & Roll Hall of Fame Induction Ceremony on November 14, 2026 in Los Angeles, California. (Photo by Gilbert Flores/Variety)
									Variety

schema.headline: Rock & Roll Hall of Fame Ceremony Gets Fired Up With Live-Wire Numbers From U2, the Chili Peppers, Usher, Cynthia Erivo, Sienna Spiro, Aerosmith and More

	“KPop Demon Hunters” is getting the Criterion treatment. Netflix’s breakout musical fantasy film is now available as a physical release, thanks to a special Blu-ray set available to buy online now.

	The film is available in Blu-ray and 4K UHD editions, priced at $39.95 and $49.95, respectively but Amazon currently has the Blu-ray version discounted by 50% off ahead of Black Friday and on the heels of the new “KPop Demon Hunters” tour announcement.


		

						
			
	

					Amazon
	
					
		

										NEW RELEASE						

					KPop Demon Hunters (The Criterion Collection) Blu-ray		

		
	

	The Criterion Collection release features the Oscar-winning animated film remastered in 4K with Dolby Atmos soundtrack. Behind-the-scenes content includes a “making of” documentary, plus lyric videos and other featurettes. The set also comes with collectible postcards with original illustrations from animators who worked on the film. The anime-inspired cover art was also created exclusively for the physical release.

	The release caps a major run for “KPop Demon Hunters,” which became one of Netflix’s biggest original film breakouts after releasing last June. Directed by Maggie Kang and Chris Appelhans and produced in partnership with Sony Pictures Animation, the film follows K-pop superstars Rumi, Mira and Zoey — voiced by Arden Cho, May Hong and Ji-young Yoo — who lead double lives as demon hunters when they aren’t selling out stadiums.

	The film, which won the Oscar for best animated feature, broke multiple records over the past year. It became the most streamed movie of 2025 while its corresponding soundtrack hit No. 1 on the Billboard 200. The lead single “Golden” remained at No. 1 on the Hot 100, with the film becoming the first soundtrack to place four songs in the chart’s top 10 at the same time.


	The film has also spawned dozens of lucrative partnerships and licensing deals. In fact, Mattel and Hasbro, fierce rivals, were named a global “co-master” toy licensee for “KPop Demon Hunters — a dual license structure believed to be unprecedented in the industry.  Themed products such as Uno, Monopoly, and dolls have begun rolling out this spring. 

		

						
			
	

					Amazon
	
					
		

										NUMBER ONE RELEASE						

					KPop Demon Hunters (The Criterion Collection) [DVD]		

		
	

	A sequel is currently in development at Netflix and Sony Pictures Animation, with Kang and Appelhans returning. The just-announced tour, meantime, puts the film’s animated K-pop trio Huntr/x in front of live audiences. Dates kick off in June.

	Billy Eva
body:
If you purchase an independently reviewed product or service through a link on our website, Variety may receive an affiliate commission.

	Billy Evans is speaking out about his portrayal in Nathan Fielder and Lance Oppenheim’s hit documentary “You Can See Everything.”

	The longtime partner of disgraced Theranos founder Elizabeth Holmes sits down with CBS News chief correspondent Matt Gutman for his first television interview on “CBS News Sunday Morning,” airing Sunday, Nov. 15, at 9 a.m. ET/PT on CBS and streaming on Paramount+.


	The interview arrives amid renewed public fascination with Holmes and Evans following the A24’s breakout documentary, which follows the couple in the weeks leading up to Holmes’ imprisonment for defrauding Theranos investors. The film has become a box office sensation, grossing more than $80 million worldwide.
	

	“I would have preferred for that not to be the case, but it’s entertainment. I didn’t get to control that edit,” Evans tells Gutman in a preview of Sunday’s interview. He adds that his primary motivation for participating was to show audiences a more personal side of Holmes, who is currently serving a federal prison sentence for fraud.

	Viewers can watch the interview live on Paramount+ with a Premium subscription, which costs $13.99 per month and includes access to a live feed of their local CBS station. The streaming service’s ad-supported Essential plan, priced at $8.99 per month, also offers CBS programming on demand, with new episodes generally available the day after broadcast.

	Sunday’s broadcast, hosted by Jane Pauley, will also feature interviews with U2 marking the band’s 50th anniversary, John Travolta discussing his upcoming film “November 1963” and author Min Jin Lee on her latest novel, “American Hagwon.”

title: Billy Evans Addresses Amanda Seyfried’s Portrayal of Elizabeth Holmes in ‘You Can See Everything’: She Was ‘Eager’ to ‘Play a Character’
description:
Billy Evans is finally weighing in on Amanda Seyfried’s portrayal of Elizabeth Holmes in “You Can See Everything.”

	In his first interview since t
body:
Billy Evans is finally weighing in on Amanda Seyfried’s portrayal of Elizabeth Holmes in “You Can See Everything.”

	In his first interview since the A24 documentary’s release last month, released Sunday morning, Holmes’ partner sat down with CBS News chief correspondent Matt Gutman to discuss how, exactly, he feels about the film. When asked what he thought about Seyfriend’s role, Evans responded: “I’m really glad that they included her because it shows what a difference there is between the real thing and how eager she was to play a character.”
	

	Gutman then followed up by questioning if the actress played the role of the disgraced tech founder well, to which Evans said that he was “glad Nathan was there to help her.” “Doesn’t seem like you hold very high opinion of her acting, or of her as a person,” noted Gutman.

	Evans concluded: “Matt, I’m gonna do my best not to speak poorly about other people right now, because I’ve had a lot of people do that about me recently, and I know how it feels.”

	Seyfriend also recently told all about her experience filming “You Can See Everything” in a new interview with Rolling Stone, including that she didn’t tell her agents about the project and had “no approval” over filming. She also noted that her opinion of Evans “only got worse” as filming went on, and she felt he “disrespected” her during that tense dinner table conversation. 

	Before hitting theaters on Oct. 16, the buzzy doc had been quietly in the works from Nathan Fielder and Lance Oppenheim for more than three years. The doc offers an unhinged look at the Theranos founder a month before she began an 11-year prison sentence for defrauding investors.
	

	In addition to being eligible for best documentary feature at the 99th Academy Awards, the film will also be submitted across the board as seen on A24’s awards site: best picture, director, production design, cinematography, costume design, film editing, makeup and hairstyling, sound and original score. Seyfried, who appears as herself while also reprising her Emmy-winning turn as Holmes from “The Dropout,” will be campaigned in the supporting actress category.

title: Thessaloniki Awards: Jacqueline Lentzou’s ‘A Day in the Life of Jo: Chapter Phaedra’ Wins the Golden Alexander
description: Jacqueline Lentzou’s “A Day in the Life of Jo: Chapter Phaedra” won the top prize Sunday at the Thessaloniki Film Festival, taking home the Golden
body:
Jacqueline Lentzou’s “A Day in the Life of Jo: Chapter Phaedra” won the top prize Sunday at the Thessaloniki Film Festival, taking home the Golden Alexander for best feature film in the Arrivals international competition section.

	The Greek filmmaker’s sophomore feature premiered in the Venice Film Festival’s Horizons strand, where it won the award for best director. It’s since gone on to play at the New York Film Festival, the BFI London Film Festival and the Busan Film Festival.
	

	Inspired by true events, “A Day in the Life of Jo” follows the unruly, melancholic 15-year-old Jo — played by newcomer Evia Andriopoulou — as she navigates the ups and downs of a typical day in a typical teenager’s life. Drifting through a series of seemingly unrelated and inconsequential events, that otherwise ordinary day is turned upside-down with the arrival of Phaedra (Anastasia Gouliamou), a bookish classmate whose warbling rendition of an old love ballad reduces Jo to tears. In an instant, her life — her drab, unremarkable day — becomes full of possibility, hurtling toward both tragedy and transformation.

	The film scooped a trio of awards on Sunday, as well as a Special Mention for Andriopoulou.

	The Silver Alexander for best director went to Pauline Julier and Nicolas Chapoulier for “Les Indes,” which had its premiere in the Venice Film Festival’s Venice Days strand. The writer-director duo’s feature debut is set in 1652 and follows three men as they transport a painting across a Europe ravaged by wars and uprisings.

	Best acting honors in the Arrivals competition went to Caique Copque and Italo Martins for “The Riverbank,” a queer erotic thriller from Brazilian directors Matheus Farias and Enock Carvalho that premiered in competition in Locarno. Best actress went to Arisa Sasaki, for Konstantina Kotzamani’s Cannes Un Certain Regard-premiering debut feature “Titanic Ocean,” an offbeat coming-of-age story set at a boarding school for aspiring mermaids in Japan.
	

	In the festival’s Meet the Neighbors+ competition section, which includes debut or sophomore films from the 36 countries of Southeastern Europe, the Mediterranean and the Middle East, the Golden Alexander for best feature went to “Dua,” by Kosovan filmmaker Blerta Basholli. Premiering in Cannes’ Critics’ Week strand, the director’s sophomore feature tells the story of a 13-year-old girl coming of age in the shadow of the Kosovo War.

	The section’s Silver Alexander for best director went to Abdallah Alkhatib for “Chronicles From the Siege.” The winner of the Berlinale’s Perspectives award for debuts, the film presents vignettes of Palestinian lives in Gaza and in refugee camps.

	The award for best actor went to Alexis Manenti and Julian Świeżewski for “Flesh and Fuel,” French filmmaker Pierre Le Gall’s story about a passionate love affair between two long-distance truck drivers. Premiering in Cannes’ Critics Week, it took the top prize at the Zurich Film Festival and also earned Le Gall an award for best screenplay Sunday in Thessaloniki. Maria Petrova, the young star of Cypriot filmmaker Myrsini Aristidou’s Sundance Audience Prize-winning “Hold Onto Me,” took home the award for best actress.

	In the Film Forward competition section showcasing innovative filmmaking, the Golden Alexander went to Hoda Taheri and Boris Hadžija’s “I Plant My Hand in the Garden,” while the Silver Alexander went to Rob Rice for “Ponderosa,” whose star Alexis Blendel won the prize for best actress. The award for Best Artistic Achievement went to Argyris Germanidis’ “Particles of Dust,” while best actor honors went to Alexis Kalofolias for “Under the Judas Tree.”

	Here’s a rundown of the winners in the Thessaloniki Film Festival’s three competition sections:

	Arrivals

	Golden Alexander: “A Day in the Life of Jo: Chapter Phaedra,” Jacqueline Lentzou

	Silver Alexander: Pauline Julier and Nicolas Chapoulier, “Les Indes”

	Best actor: Caique Copque and Italo Martins, “The Riverbank”

	Best actress: Arisa Sasaki, “Titanic Ocean”

	Special Mention: Evita Andriopoulou, “A Day in the Life of Jo: Chapter Phaedra”

	Meet the Neighbors+

	Golden Alexander: “Dua,” Blerta Basholli
	

	Silver Alexander: Abdallah Alkhatib, “Chronicles From the Siege”

	Best actor: Alexis Manenti and Julian Świeżewski, “Flesh and Fuel”

	Best actress: Maria Petrova, “Hold Onto Me”

	Best screenplay: “Flesh and Fuel,” Pierre Le Gall

	Film Forward

	Golden Alexander: “I Plant My Hand in the Garden,” Hoda Taheri and Boris Hadžija

	Silver Alexander: Rob Rice, “Ponderosa”

	Best artistic achievement: “Particles of Dust,” Argyris Germanidis

	Best actress: Alexis Blendel, “Ponderosa”

	Best actor: Alexis Kalofolias, “Under the Judas Tree”

Finding the perfect holiday gift for the tech enthusiast in your life can be tricky, especially when they’re already equipped with the latest smartphones, headphones and smart home gadgets. But this year’s most giftable electronics go beyond the usual upgrades, offering new ways to capture memories, stream entertainment and track wellness. Best Buy is the best online retailer for holiday shopping because of its My Best Buy Plus, the retailer’s $29.99 annual membership, which offers exclusive member pricing on select products, 1% back in rewards on eligible purchases, free two-day shipping and an extended 60-day return and exchange window on most items. The membership also provides access to members-only sales and offers, making it particularly useful for anyone planning to check several names off their holiday shopping list. Below, find four tech gifts worth splurging on this holiday season: For the aspiring filmmaker or content creator, Insta360’s X5 action camera offers a considerable upgrade from traditional smartphone footage. Equipped with dual sensors and 8K 360-degree video recording, the pocket-sized device captures everything happening around the user, allowing them to choose their framing after filming. Its AI-powered editing features make it easier to transform raw footage into polished videos, while an invisible selfie-stick effect creates cinematic, third-person perspectives without requiring an actual camera operator. It’s an especially clever gift for travelers, outdoor adventurers and anyone looking to elevate their TikTok or YouTube content. For the urban commuter who’s tired of public transportation, Segway’s Max G3 electric scooter offers a faster, more flexible way to get around. The high-performance model boasts a top speed of up to 28 mph and a maximum advertised range of 50 miles on a single charge, along with a suspension system designed to smooth out uneven city streets. It also features built-in Apple Find My integration, making it easier to locate the scooter when it’s parked. It’s a practical splurge for the person who’s always on the move, provided local riding regulations allow it. EDITOR’S PICK Bose QuietComfort Ultra Headphones (2nd Gen) A reliable pair of noise-canceling headphones is a holiday gift that’s almost impossible to get wrong, particularly when they come from Bose. The second generation of the brand’s QuietComfort Ultra headphones combines premium sound quality with advanced noise cancellation and a lightweight, cushioned design that’s comfortable enough for long flights or marathon listening sessions. Bose’s Immersive Audio technology adds a spatial dimension to music, while the headphones’ new Cinema Mode is designed to make movies and television shows sound more immersive. With up to 30 hours of battery life under standard listening conditions, they’re a worthwhile upgrade for music lovers, frequent flyers and dedicated binge-watchers alike. For the wellness enthusiast who already owns every fitness gadget imaginable, Oura‘s smart ring packs an impressive amount of health-tracking technology into a piece of everyday jewelry. The sleek titanium ring monitors sleep, activity, heart rate and recovery, translating the data into personalized insights through the Oura app. Unlike a bulky smartwatch, its discreet design makes it easy to wear around the clock, whether at the gym, in the office or in bed. Available in multiple metallic finishes, it’s an especially stylish option for anyone interested in understanding their daily habits. Keep in mind that a separate Oura membership is required to unlock the device’s full range of insights.

                          UPS Cargo Jet Collides With Commercial Airplane
body:
Miami Airport
                          UPS Cargo Jet Collides With Commercial Airplane
                          'Somebody Hit Us'
                      
                  
                                                                        Published 
                              November 15, 2026
                            7:35 AM PST
                                                                            
      
    
                  
          
                          
                
                  
      
    
            A commercial airplane clipped the nose of a UPS cargo jet in Miami International Airport ... leaving two people injured.
      
    
      
      @N3lly_Nel is the original poster of this video. https://t.co/6Ee6BOGD6m
              @RSenatorFeed
          
  
    
            The incident went down Saturday night ... with a Copa Airlines pilot telling Air Traffic Control that "somebody hit us" just after its left wing clipped the UPS flight bound for Bogotá, Colombia.
      
    
            In the audio ... the UPS cargo flight's pilot admitted to going "too far" on the runway before the Copa Airlines flight "clipped us with his wing."
      

            Miami International Airport spokesperson has since shared that flights were redirected to other runways and that two patients received care from Miami-Dade Fire Rescue ... the California Post reported.
      
    
            This isn't the only traffic woe for jet-setters this weekend.
      
    
            As you know ... the FAA issued a ground stop for all flights over several hours on Friday due to "extraordinary circumstances" -- which Sean Duffy ultimately blamed on "old legacy equipment."
